subject: Oceanography
title: Density and Stratification
description: Learn Density and Stratification in one minute.

hook.text: Cold salty water sinks; warm fresh water floats. This simple rule drives the entire ocean.

buildup.text: Ocean density depends on temperature, salinity, and pressure—the 'big three' of seawater.

discovery.text: Denser water sinks beneath lighter water, creating stable layers called stratification.

twist.text: When surface water becomes very cold and salty (polar regions), it sinks thousands of meters.

climax.text: This sinking drives a global circulation that takes 1,000 years for water to complete.

punchline.text: Density differences power the ocean's deepest currents.
